title: A struck-out branch silently resumes spending 24h later, and never pages again
description:
The Phase 4 final review's one HIGH finding, in the epic's own highest-declared-risk loop, and confirmed by the reviewer reading the code.

cloud/factory/src/ci-remediation.ts:672-696 (strikeBudget), :705-743 (escalate), :939-959 (dispatch order). Schema migrations/0010_ci_remediation.sql: the ci_escalation table, PK (project, branch), has TWO WRITE SITES AND ZERO READS. grep it.

MECHANISM. strikeBudget counts ci_remediation_attempt rows in a ROLLING 24h window. Three dispatches inside it strike the branch out, escalate() opens a durable row once and sends one Telegram message. Correct so far, and tested.

What is missing is that remediateCheckFailure never checks whether (project, branch) already has an OPEN ci_escalation row before re-running strikeBudget. So as soon as the OLDEST of the three strikes ages out of the sliding window, strikeBudget answers within_budget again and the branch silently starts accepting new WRITE-grade dispatches. And because escalate() dedups on INSERT OR IGNORE against the row that already exists, 'opened' comes back false and NO FURTHER MESSAGE IS EVER SENT.

So the failure mode is: a branch the factory already gave up on quietly resumes spending a day later, with write access, and the human who was paged once is never told again. That is the precise shape an autonomy epic exists to prevent — the strike budget bounds each window and does not bound the branch.

The existing test 'escalates once, however many failures keep arriving afterward' passes because it never advances the clock past STRIKE_WINDOW_MS. grep STRIKE_WINDOW in ci-remediation.test.ts returns nothing.

ALSO IN SCOPE, two more from the same review:
- NO TOP-LEVEL CATCH on checkRunWebhookRoute (or remediateCheckFailure): an unexpected throw becomes an unhandled 5xx and BYPASSES the loop's own escalation mechanism, so the one path that is supposed to page a human is the one that does not when something unforeseen breaks. Write a durable, alertable failure record instead.
- epicOfBranch's single-pass prefix strip (low severity, no current exploit) — clean it up while you are in the file.

Fix direction for the main finding: check for an open ci_escalation row before re-evaluating the strike budget, and add the clock-advancing test that the existing suite lacks. Decide deliberately what REOPENS an escalated branch — a human clearing it is the obvious answer, and 'time passes' is the answer that caused this.

acceptance_criteria: A branch struck out and escalated does not accept new dispatches when the strike window rolls over; whatever reopens it is explicit and human-driven, not the clock. A clock-advancing test pins it. An unexpected throw in the CI webhook path produces a durable alertable record rather than an unhandled 5xx.
closed_reason: Completed: an escalated CI branch is released by a person, never by the clock. The ci_escalation table — which had two write sites and zero reads — is now consulted before the strike budget is re-evaluated, so a struck-out branch cannot silently resume write-grade dispatches when the rolling window rolls over, and the human who was paged once is not left believing it stayed stopped. Pinned by the clock-advancing test the suite lacked. Also: an unexpected throw on the CI webhook path now leaves a durable alertable fault record instead of an unhandled 5xx that bypassed the loop's own escalation.
